findings.where: Screen 11 (Turning speed), its caption, and the explain text
findings.what: "Power is torque times ω" rests on "Textbooks add" with no source in the lesson's list, and 400 kN m at 400 rev/min giving 16.76 MW is Bird's cited ship-shaft example (brief notes 7.5) yet the caption calls it "Example figures"; add the P = ωT source (MTU or Bird, notes 7.5) and name the figures as Bird's.

The picture keeps room for the rows of working, so until he answers there is an empty band about a third of a phone screen tall between the picture and the answer buttons (seen on step 2 at 360 px light and dark, and on step 14 at 360 and 1280 px).

findings.where: Screen 7 (Degrees and radians), text and rows
findings.what: The screen goes from "stops at 213.0°, left of the centre and below it" to "cos 10 = −0.839" without the link between them; one clause pointing back to lesson 3 (the cosine is the arm's shadow across, which is negative left of the centre) would complete the why.

findings.where: Screen 5's after-line and the practice list
findings.what: Multiplying by π ÷ 180 to turn degrees into radians is stated but never derived; one line ("180° = π radians, so 1° is π ÷ 180 radians") would close the step, the way 180 ÷ π is already worked out for one radian.
The picture opens as a bare circle with only the centre pin for about 1.3 s, and nothing is drawn for the two conversion rows (60° and 2 radians); the picture only shows 10° against 10 radians.

findings.where: Screen 7 text and the explain text
findings.what: The rule that no degree sign means radians, and the line about calculus with sine and cosine, also rest on "Textbooks add" with no listed source (brief: SQA Higher notes 2.2, Lamar notes 6.2), and the calculus line does not say which course it belongs to (Derivatives, in Advanced maths).
ω first appears without a name; say "ω, the Greek letter omega" once, because lesson 6 depends on it.

findings.where: Step 8's Why? and the practice size check
findings.what: "About 57.3 times smaller than the degree figure" is loose wording; "the degree figure is about 57.3 times the radian figure" says it exactly.

The rod (navy #17324D, 7 px) and the arm (slate #1F2937, 5 px) are almost the same colour, so in the opening still the rod lying on the arm cannot be seen as a separate copy, and once it is laid only its width tells it apart; a pale core or outline on the rod would make it readable at a glance.
The "0.25 m" radius label sits right against the centre pin at 360 px and at 1280 px; move it a few units out along the arm.
